Get started

Add Odin to an existing project

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Install the addonCreate a scripts packageCompile the scriptsWork with the editorAdd a multiplayer framework

An existing Godot project needs the core extension, a scripts package, and a build command. Its scenes and assets can stay in their current layout. The installed addon supplies engine bindings and build helpers; your project owns its scripts and generated library.

Install the addon#

Copy the distributable's addons/odin_godot directory into the project's res://addons/. Godot discovers its .gdextension manifest when the project opens. Use the manifest and native binaries from the same distribution.

If you are building the core yourself, follow the full wiring guide. The native core library registers Odin with Godot and loads the separate scripts library.

Create a scripts package#

Create a scripts/ directory and add an Odin script. All .odin files in this directory use the same package name. Copy the addon's ordinary starter scripts when you want a working scene to modify; use the optional Replay starter when you want a complete-world simulation.

The build generates the boot registration normally required to initialize the script library. Keep custom registration only when the project intentionally owns that setup. Your first script shows a small attached node.

Compile the scripts#

Run this from your project's root, replacing the addon path if necessary:

Shell
ODIN_GODOT_ROOT="$PWD/addons/odin_godot" SKIP_CORE=1 \
  bash addons/odin_godot/build/build_scripts.sh .

SKIP_CORE=1 uses the addon's prebuilt core. The script library is written under the project's bin/, using the platform's shared-library extension. An Odin compiler must be available on PATH, or configured in the editor's settings.

For a checkout-based build, use the checkout's build/build_scripts.sh and pass the game directory as its first argument. Set ODIN_GODOT_ROOT or the editor's odin_godot/root consistently so imports resolve to the same SDK.

Work with the editor#

Attach an .odin file directly to a matching node type. Inspector exports, signals, animation callbacks, and typed engine calls use the regular authoring surface. Use reload-on-save and editor settings to configure the development loop.

The scripts are compiled ahead of time. Changing code or exported layout requires a rebuild. For a loader failure, read the engine's library error and check that the scripts library, core, and compiler ABI are compatible before changing gameplay.

Add a multiplayer framework#

Kit and Replay are optional imports. Kit integrates field declarations with script entities; Replay puts the mutable simulation in a separate pure Odin model. Choose the state and authority model before splitting gameplay between nodes and shared state.

For larger games, script modules provide independently built script packages. Use them when rebuild boundaries matter; a small project can start with one scripts package.
